chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Mu'awiya, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' (the final circumambulation) until he returned to his family. He said: 'Women are not permissible to him until he visits the House (performs Tawaf al-Nisa'). If he dies, his heir or anyone else may perform it on his behalf. As for while he is alive, it is not suitable for anyone else to perform it on his behalf. And if he forgot the throwing of the Jamarat, the two are not equal; throwing is Sunnah and Tawaf is Fard (obligatory).'

key_terms.رَمْيَ ٱلْجِمَارِ: Throwing of the Jamarat (stones at the pillars in Mina)
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: Sunnah, a recommended but non-obligatory act
key_terms.طَوَافَ ٱلنِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba required before leaving Mecca
key_terms.يَزُورَ ٱلْبَيْتَ: Visits the House, referring to performing the specific circumambulation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets the final Tawaf before leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of *Tawaf al-Nisa'* (the final circumambulation) as a mandatory pillar (*Fard*) rather than a mere sunnah, distinguishing it from the throwing of stones (*Ramy al-Jamarat*). It establishes that while a living pilgrim must personally complete this act to permit marital relations, a proxy may perform it on their behalf if they die before doing so, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the transferability of ritual obligations.
